passages.text: Weight gain of more than 2 kg (about 4-5 lb) in 2 to 3 days can signal fluid buildup in heart failure and needs urgent clinician contact.
New or worsening shortness of breath at rest, or waking at night gasping for air, is a heart-failure danger sign requiring urgent care.
Increasing swelling of the ankles, legs, or abdomen indicates worsening fluid retention and should be reported promptly.
Chest pain or pressure, especially with sweating or nausea, may indicate a cardiac emergency; call emergency services immediately.
Severe dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting can reflect dangerously low blood pressure or an abnormal heart rhythm and needs urgent evaluation.
New confusion, marked fatigue, or reduced alertness can be a sign of poor heart output and warrants urgent medical attention.
Furosemide is a loop diuretic used to remove excess fluid in heart failure. Take it in the morning to avoid nighttime urination; report muscle cramps or excessive thirst.
Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor that lowers blood pressure and reduces strain on the heart. A dry cough or dizziness can occur; do not stop without advice.
Carvedilol is a beta-blocker that slows the heart and improves heart-failure survival. Take with food; do not stop suddenly as this can worsen symptoms.
Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic used in heart failure. Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes; report irregular heartbeat.
Dapagliflozin is an SGLT2 inhibitor shown to reduce heart-failure hospitalizations. Maintain hydration and report signs of urinary or genital infection.
Limiting dietary sodium (salt) helps prevent fluid buildup; aim for the intake target your care team specifies.
Weigh yourself each morning after using the bathroom and before breakfast, and record it to catch fluid gain early.
Follow any fluid-intake limit set by your care team, and space drinks through the day to manage thirst.
Albuterol is used for asthma rescue inhaler: relieves acute asthma symptoms by relaxing airway muscles; overuse can cause tremor or fast heartbeat.
Metformin is used for type 2 diabetes: lowers glucose production by the liver; take with meals to reduce stomach upset.
Levothyroxine is used for hypothyroidism: replaces thyroid hormone; take on an empty stomach and separate it from calcium and iron.
Warfarin is used for anticoagulation: an anticoagulant requiring regular INR monitoring; many foods and drugs alter its effect.
Atorvastatin is used for high cholesterol: lowers LDL cholesterol; report unexplained muscle pain or weakness.
Omeprazole is used for acid reflux: reduces stomach acid for reflux and ulcers; long-term use is reviewed periodically.
Amoxicillin is used for bacterial infection: a penicillin-class antibiotic; complete the full prescribed course.
Sumatriptan is used for migraine: treats migraine attacks by narrowing blood vessels around the brain; not for prevention.
Tiotropium is used for COPD maintenance: a long-acting inhaled bronchodilator for maintenance treatment of COPD.
Sertraline is used for depression: an SSRI antidepressant; effects take several weeks and it should not be stopped abruptly.
Alendronate is used for osteoporosis: a bisphosphonate; take with water and remain upright for 30 minutes.
Allopurinol is used for gout prevention: lowers uric acid to prevent gout attacks; drink adequate fluids and report any rash.
Levetiracetam is used for epilepsy: an antiseizure medication; report mood changes and do not stop suddenly.
Cetirizine is used for allergic rhinitis: a second-generation antihistamine causing less drowsiness than older agents.
Ibuprofen is used for pain and inflammation: an NSAID that can worsen fluid retention and kidney function and is often avoided in heart failure.
Gabapentin is used for nerve pain: used for neuropathic pain and some seizures; may cause drowsiness and dizziness.
Amlodipine is used for hypertension: a calcium-channel blocker for blood pressure; ankle swelling is a common side effect.
Hydrochlorothiazide is used for hypertension: a thiazide diuretic for blood pressure; can lower potassium and raise blood sugar.
Prednisone is used for inflammation: a corticosteroid; do not stop abruptly and watch for raised blood sugar and mood changes.
Insulin glargine is used for diabetes: a long-acting basal insulin; rotate injection sites and watch for low blood sugar.
Montelukast is used for asthma/allergy: a leukotriene modifier taken in the evening for asthma and allergic rhinitis.
Clopidogrel is used for antiplatelet: reduces clot risk after stents; report unusual bruising or bleeding.
Apixaban is used for anticoagulation: a direct oral anticoagulant; do not miss doses and report bleeding.
Digoxin is used for rate control: narrow therapeutic range; report nausea, visual changes, or slow heartbeat.
Tamsulosin is used for enlarged prostate: relaxes bladder-neck muscles; may cause dizziness when standing.
Finasteride is used for enlarged prostate: shrinks the prostate over months; handle with care in pregnancy.
Escitalopram is used for anxiety: an SSRI for anxiety and depression; taper rather than stopping suddenly.
Pantoprazole is used for reflux: a proton-pump inhibitor for reflux and ulcers.
Azithromycin is used for respiratory infection: a macrolide antibiotic; can affect heart rhythm in susceptible people.
Ciprofloxacin is used for urinary infection: a fluoroquinolone antibiotic; report tendon pain and avoid with dairy at dosing.
Warfarin sodium is used for anticoagulation: same active drug as warfarin; keep vitamin-K intake steady.
Methotrexate is used for rheumatoid arthritis: a weekly disease-modifying drug; NEVER take daily; take folic acid as directed.
Hydroxychloroquine is used for lupus/RA: used for autoimmune disease; eye checks are recommended periodically.
Salbutamol is used for asthma: another name for albuterol; a short-acting reliever inhaler.
Budesonide is used for asthma maintenance: an inhaled corticosteroid; rinse the mouth after use to prevent thrush.
Rivaroxaban is used for anticoagulation: a direct oral anticoagulant taken with food; report bleeding.
Empagliflozin is used for diabetes: an SGLT2 inhibitor for diabetes; maintain hydration and genital hygiene.
Glipizide is used for type 2 diabetes: a sulfonylurea that can cause low blood sugar; take before meals.
Losartan is used for hypertension: an ARB for blood pressure; monitor potassium and kidney function.
Propranolol is used for tremor/migraine: a non-selective beta-blocker used for tremor and migraine prevention.
Nitroglycerin is used for angina: relieves chest pain from angina; sit down when using and seek help if pain persists.
Aspirin is used for antiplatelet: low-dose aspirin reduces clot risk; report black stools or easy bruising.
Codeine is used for cough/pain: an opioid for pain or cough; can cause drowsiness and constipation.
Diazepam is used for anxiety/spasm: a benzodiazepine; causes drowsiness and can be habit-forming.
Fluticasone is used for allergic rhinitis: a steroid nasal spray; use daily for best allergy control.
Ranitidine is used for reflux: an H2 blocker historically used for reflux and ulcers.
Simvastatin is used for high cholesterol: a statin; certain doses interact with other drugs, so follow labeling.
Enoxaparin is used for clot prevention: an injectable low-molecular-weight heparin; rotate injection sites.
Carbamazepine is used for epilepsy: an antiseizure drug with many interactions; report rash promptly.
Venlafaxine is used for depression: an SNRI; taper slowly to avoid discontinuation symptoms.
Olanzapine is used for psychiatric: an antipsychotic that can raise blood sugar and weight.
Mirtazapine is used for depression: an antidepressant that can increase appetite and cause drowsiness.
Dabigatran is used for anticoagulation: a direct oral anticoagulant; keep in original packaging for stability.
Febuxostat is used for gout: lowers uric acid as an alternative to allopurinol.
Colchicine is used for gout flare: eases acute gout; diarrhea is a common dose-limiting effect.
Naproxen is used for pain: an NSAID like ibuprofen; can worsen fluid retention and is often avoided in heart failure.
Dexamethasone is used for inflammation: a potent corticosteroid; monitor blood sugar and mood.
Furosemide 10mg/ml is used for loop diuretic solution: a liquid formulation for people who cannot swallow tablets.
Acetaminophen is used for pain/fever: paracetamol for pain and fever; stay within the daily maximum to protect the liver.
Doxycycline is used for infection: a tetracycline antibiotic; avoid lying down right after dosing.
